result.title: Log-Derivative Trick for Parametric Markov Chains
result.summary:
Optimizing expected rewards and reachability probabilities in parametric Markov chains (pMCs) is central to the analysis and synthesis of probabilistic systems with loops. While traditional symbolic synthesis approaches--such as parameter lifting and rational function generation--suffer from scalability bottlenecks, gradient-based optimization emerges as an effective alternative. However, existing gradient-based techniques still rely on symbolic gradient computation--such as solving large linear systems--over the global state space, inheriting scalability limits. Finite-horizon approximation is possible but introduces uncontrollable bias.
  In this paper, we introduce a scalable Monte Carlo gradient estimator based on a measure-theoretic generalization of the log-derivative trick. We prove that our estimator provides unbiased gradient estimates under almost-sure termination and standard regularity conditions. Crucially, our method avoids global state-space materialization and linear system solving entirely: it operates purely along sampled trajectories, requiring only black-box evaluations of local transition probabilities (or densities) and their derivatives. Unlike existing pMC techniques that are fundamentally restricted to finite discrete systems, our measure-theoretic framework naturally extends to continuous and general $σ$-finite state spaces. Empirical evaluations on synthetic discrete pMCs and continuous-state case studies demonstrate that our method scales to state spaces far beyond the reach of existing solvers, significantly reducing execution time without introducing bias.

AI.brief_summary: 论文将 log-derivative trick 推广到测度论形式，提出一种沿采样轨迹工作的蒙特卡洛梯度估计器，用于优化参数化马尔可夫链的期望奖励与可达概率，并在几乎必然终止等条件下证明估计无偏，避免显式构建全局状态空间与求解线性系统。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「仅沿采样轨迹、只对局部转移做黑盒求值」的无偏梯度估计，可能为 latent 推理轨迹上的贡献分配与训练监督提供可核查的方法线索，但该工作面向概率系统分析，迁移到 VLM 推理的可行性仍需判断。
